jp: 母[はは]{も|mo-both}父[ちち]{も|mo-both}先生[せんせい]です。
en: My mother and my father are both teachers.
why: も after each noun says both A and B share the same predicate.

jp: 今日[きょう]{は|wa-topic}朝[あさ]{も|mo-both}夜[よる]{も|mo-both}雨[あめ]でした。
en: Today it rained both in the morning and at night.
why: Repeating も after both time words means it was rainy in both.

jp: 犬[いぬ]{も|mo-both}猫[ねこ]{も|mo-both}大好[だいす]きです。
en: I love both dogs and cats.
why: AもBも puts both items under one predicate; the second も is required.

jp: 兄[あに]{も|mo-both}姉[あね]{も|mo-both}東京[とうきょう]{に|ni-location}住[す]んでいます。
en: My older brother and my older sister both live in Tokyo.
why: Both people share the verb, so each noun takes も.

jp: この町[まち]{は|wa-topic}夏[なつ]{も|mo-both}冬[ふゆ]{も|mo-both}人[ひと]{が|ga-subject}多[おお]いです。
en: In this town there are lots of people in both summer and winter.
why: Summer and winter are both true cases, so each gets も.

jp: コーヒー{も|mo-both}紅茶[こうちゃ]{も|mo-both}飲[の]みません。
en: I drink neither coffee nor tea.
why: With a negative verb, AもBも means neither A nor B.

jp: 田中[たなか]さん{も|mo-both}山田[やまだ]さん{も|mo-both}来[き]ませんでした。
en: Neither Mr. Tanaka nor Mr. Yamada came.
why: Two people joined by も…も with a negative verb: neither of them.

jp: 駅[えき]{の|no-possessive}前[まえ]{に|ni-location}銀行[ぎんこう]{も|mo-both}郵便局[ゆうびんきょく]{も|mo-both}あります。
en: In front of the station there are both a bank and a post office.
why: Both places exist, so each noun is followed by も.

jp: 弟[おとうと]{は|wa-topic}英語[えいご]{も|mo-both}数学[すうがく]{も|mo-both}好[す]きです。
en: My younger brother likes both English and math.
why: も…も joins two subjects he likes, giving both A and B.

jp: 彼女[かのじょ]{は|wa-topic}歌[うた]{も|mo-both}ダンス{も|mo-both}上手[じょうず]です。
en: She is good at both singing and dancing.
why: Each skill gets も to say she is good at both.

jp: 朝[あさ]{は|wa-topic}パン{も|mo-both}ごはん{も|mo-both}食[た]べます。
en: In the morning I eat both bread and rice.
why: Both foods are eaten, so each is marked with も.

jp: 昨日[きのう]{は|wa-topic}風[かぜ]{も|mo-both}雨[あめ]{も|mo-both}強[つよ]かったです。
en: Yesterday both the wind and the rain were strong.
why: The wind and the rain both had the property, so も follows each.

jp: この本[ほん]{は|wa-topic}絵[え]{も|mo-both}文字[もじ]{も|mo-both}大[おお]きいです。
en: In this book, both the pictures and the letters are big.
why: も…も states that the same description holds for both nouns.

jp: 兄[あに]{は|wa-topic}サッカー{も|mo-both}野球[やきゅう]{も|mo-both}します。
en: My older brother plays both soccer and baseball.
why: He does both sports; each sport takes も.

jp: 父[ちち]{は|wa-topic}お酒[さけ]{も|mo-both}たばこ{も|mo-both}やめました。
en: My father gave up both drinking and smoking.
why: Both things were given up, so each is marked with も.

jp: 公園[こうえん]{で|de-place}{も|mo-both}図書館[としょかん]{で|de-place}{も|mo-both}勉強[べんきょう]できます。
en: You can study both in the park and in the library.
why: で and も stack: 公園でも図書館でも means in both places.

jp: 姉[あね]{に|ni-recipient}{も|mo-both}母[はは]{に|ni-recipient}{も|mo-both}手紙[てがみ]{を|o-object}書[か]きました。
en: I wrote letters to both my sister and my mother.
why: に + も is repeated for each recipient to mean both.

jp: トマト{も|mo-both}きゅうり{も|mo-both}好[す]きじゃありません。
en: I like neither tomatoes nor cucumbers.
why: With a negative predicate, AもBも means neither A nor B.

jp: スーパー{で|de-place}牛乳[ぎゅうにゅう]{も|mo-both}卵[たまご]{も|mo-both}買[か]いました。
en: I bought both milk and eggs at the supermarket.
why: Two items bought together: each noun takes も.

jp: 昨夜[ゆうべ]{は|wa-topic}頭[あたま]{も|mo-both}おなか{も|mo-both}痛[いた]かったです。
en: Last night both my head and my stomach hurt.
why: Both body parts hurt, so each is followed by も.

jp: 私[わたし]{の|no-possessive}部屋[へや]{に|ni-location}テレビ{も|mo-both}ラジオ{も|mo-both}ありません。
en: There is neither a TV nor a radio in my room.
why: With ありません, AもBも means neither one exists.

jp: 山田[やまだ]さん{も|mo-both}鈴木[すずき]さん{も|mo-both}パーティー{に/へ|ni-destination}行[い]きました。
en: Both Mr. Yamada and Mr. Suzuki went to the party.
why: Both people did the same action, so each is marked with も.

jp: あの子[こ]{は|wa-topic}頭[あたま]{も|mo-both}性格[せいかく]{も|mo-both}いいです。
en: That child is both smart and good-natured.
why: も…も adds both qualities to the same person.

jp: 母[はは]{は|wa-topic}英語[えいご]{も|mo-both}フランス語[ご]{も|mo-both}話[はな]せます。
en: My mother can speak both English and French.
why: Both languages are spoken, so each noun takes も.

jp: 祖父[そふ]{は|wa-topic}目[め]{も|mo-both}耳[みみ]{も|mo-both}よくありません。
en: My grandfather's eyes and ears are both poor.
why: With a negative predicate, AもBも says the same bad condition applies to both A and B.

jp: この映画[えいが]{は|wa-topic}子供[こども]{も|mo-both}大人[おとな]{も|mo-both}楽[たの]しめます。
en: Both children and adults can enjoy this movie.
why: も…も joins two groups that both enjoy it.

jp: 木曜日[もくようび]{も|mo-both}金曜日[きんようび]{も|mo-both}休[やす]みです。
en: Both Thursday and Friday are days off.
why: Both days share the predicate, so each gets も.

jp: 私[わたし]たち{は|wa-topic}昼[ひる]{も|mo-both}夜[よる]{も|mo-both}働[はたら]きました。
en: We worked both day and night.
why: Both periods apply, so each time word takes も.

jp: この店[みせ]{は|wa-topic}ケーキ{も|mo-both}クッキー{も|mo-both}おいしいです。
en: At this shop both the cake and the cookies are delicious.
why: Both items are described by the same adjective, so も follows each.

jp: 新[あたら]しい先生[せんせい]{は|wa-topic}英語[えいご]{も|mo-both}中国語[ちゅうごくご]{も|mo-both}教[おし]えます。
en: The new teacher teaches both English and Chinese.
why: Both subjects are taught, so each is marked with も.

jp: バス{も|mo-both}電車[でんしゃ]{も|mo-both}使[つか]いません。
en: I use neither buses nor trains.
why: With a negative verb, AもBも means neither A nor B.

jp: 彼[かれ]{は|wa-topic}肉[にく]{も|mo-both}野菜[やさい]{も|mo-both}食[た]べません。
en: He eats neither meat nor vegetables.
why: With a negative verb, も…も means he eats neither.
